questions.q: Which system table records billable usage in DBUs?

options.t: `system.access.audit`, which logs every billable action
`system.billing.usage`
`system.query.history`, which totals the DBUs of each query
`system.compute.clusters`, which holds the hourly DBU totals
options.why: Compute tables describe compute, not usage records.

questions.explain: system.billing.usage holds billable usage in DBUs (records usually within 12 hours); join it with system.billing.list_prices to estimate cost.

questions.q: Which column of system.billing.usage attributes usage to a job?

options.t: `usage_date`, combined with the job's schedule
`usage_quantity`, divided by the number of jobs
`usage_metadata.job_id`
`sku_name`, which names the job that used the compute

questions.explain: The billing page's examples use usage_date, sku_name, usage_quantity and usage_metadata.job_id.

questions.q: A team plans to copy system tables to an external warehouse every night for reporting. What does Databricks say about exporting them?

options.t: It is required, since system tables keep 7 days only
options.why: Retention differs by table; audit keeps 365 days free.

options.t: It is allowed only for the audit table, which isn't sensitive
It is the recommended way to report on usage across the account
It highly discourages exporting system table data outside the platform

questions.explain: Databricks highly discourages exporting system table data outside the platform.

questions.q: How do you query a declarative pipeline's progress and data quality results?

options.t: Query `event_log(<pipeline id>)`, or the pipeline_events system table
Run DESCRIBE HISTORY on each table the pipeline writes
options.why: History shows writes, not the pipeline's quality metrics.

options.t: Open the Spark UI's Streaming tab for the pipeline
options.why: Not the documented source of these metrics.

options.t: Read the pipeline's checkpoint folder in its storage location, which holds the metrics

questions.explain: Every pipeline writes an event log to a hidden Delta table: query it with event_log(<pipelineId>), or use the pipeline_events system table across pipelines. Don't delete the event log.

questions.q: Several engineers need to query a pipeline's event log with event_log(). By default, who can?

options.t: Anyone with SELECT on the pipeline's tables
options.why: Table privileges don't open the event log.

options.t: Only the pipeline's run-as user
Only metastore admins
Every workspace user
options.why: By default only the run-as user can.

questions.explain: Query the event log with SELECT * FROM event_log(<pipelineId>); by default only the run-as user can. Databricks recommends the pipeline_events system table (Beta) across pipelines.

questions.q: A task fails, is retried and then succeeds. The job has a failure notification at job level. What does the on-call engineer receive?

options.t: A success notification, always
options.why: Only if success notifications are configured.

options.t: A notification for the first failure, then nothing for the success
options.why: Job-level notifications aren't sent for retried tasks.

options.t: Nothing: job-level notifications aren't sent for retried tasks
Two notifications, one per attempt

questions.explain: Job-level notifications aren't sent for retried tasks; use task notifications to hear about every failure.

questions.q: A stream falls behind. Which job notification fits, and how is it measured?

options.t: A duration warning on the task, which fires once a day when the stream is late
options.why: Duration warnings are about run time.

options.t: A failure notification, which fires when lag exceeds the threshold
A SQL alert on the Spark UI
options.why: The Spark UI isn't a query source for alerts.

options.t: A streaming backlog notification: a 10-minute average, repeated every 30 minutes

questions.explain: Job notifications cover streaming backlog over a threshold; backlog alerts use a 10-minute average and repeat every 30 minutes.

questions.q: What are the states of a current Databricks SQL alert?

options.t: OK, TRIGGERED and ERROR
GREEN, AMBER and RED
OK, TRIGGERED and UNKNOWN
RUNNING, FAILED and SUCCEEDED

questions.explain: SQL alerts run a query on a schedule and notify on a condition; states are OK, TRIGGERED and ERROR; legacy alerts' UNKNOWN status is gone.

questions.q: A job must run a remediation task only when a data-quality alert fires. How?

options.t: Use a For each task over the alert's rows
options.why: For each iterates; it doesn't branch on alert state.

options.t: Add the alert as a SQL alert task; later tasks branch on its result
Point the alert's webhook destination at the job's Run now URL so the job starts
Set the remediation task's Run if to All done

questions.explain: An alert can run as a job task so later tasks branch on it.

questions.q: A query is slow and you suspect an exploding join. Where do you look?

options.t: The pipeline event log
options.why: This is an ad hoc query.

options.t: system.billing.usage for the warehouse
The query profile: the operator graph with time, rows and memory per operator
DESCRIBE DETAIL on each table in the query, comparing their file counts

questions.explain: The query profile shows each operator's time, rows and memory, a Top operators panel and insights, including exploding joins or full scans. It isn't available for results from the query cache.

questions.q: A query was answered from the query result cache. Can you open its query profile?

options.t: Yes, it is always available
Yes, but only as an image
Only with ownership of the warehouse that answered the query from its cache
options.why: Ownership or CAN MONITOR is needed in general; cached results have no profile.

options.t: No: profiles aren't available for results served from the query cache

questions.explain: The query profile is not available for queries answered from the query cache, and needs ownership or CAN MONITOR on the warehouse.

questions.q: In the Spark UI's Streaming tab, what suggests a backlog is building?

options.t: Batches taking more than about 80% of the trigger interval
More than 200 tasks per batch, the default number of shuffle partitions
An input rate higher than zero
A checkpoint folder larger than 1 GB

questions.explain: A batch should finish within about 80% of the batch interval, or a backlog builds.

questions.q: Which system table holds audit events, and how long are they kept free?

options.t: system.billing.usage, 30 days, then archived
system.access.audit, 365 days
system.lakeflow.jobs, 90 days
system.query.history, forever

questions.explain: system.access.audit holds audit events with 365 days of free retention.

questions.q: Before dropping a silver column, a team wants every table and dashboard query that uses it. Where?

options.t: SHOW GRANTS on the column
The table's comment
Column-level lineage, in Catalog Explorer or system.access.column_lineage
DESCRIBE HISTORY on the silver table, which lists every query that read it

questions.explain: Lineage is captured automatically down to column level, across workspaces on the metastore, and queryable in system.access.table_lineage and column_lineage.

questions.q: In a job's matrix view, what does a pink bar mean?

options.t: Waiting for retry
Failed
Succeeded
Skipped

questions.explain: Run bars are coloured by status: green success, red failure, pink skipped, yellow waiting for retry, grey pending, cancelled or timed out.

questions.q: An hourly job's runs take 90 minutes, and every other hourly run is missing from history. Why?

options.t: Runs beyond maximum concurrent runs (default one) are skipped
Failed runs are hidden in the matrix view
The job's timeout cancels them silently
The scheduler rounds the hourly schedule to two hours whenever the workspace is under load

questions.explain: By default a job runs one run at a time and runs beyond maximum concurrent runs are skipped; fix the duration or raise the limit if overlap is safe.

questions.q: Which system tables describe Lakeflow job runs across the account?

options.t: system.billing.list_prices
system.lakeflow.jobs, job_tasks and job_run_timeline
system.access.audit only, filtered to the jobs service
options.why: Audit records events, not run timelines.

options.t: system.compute.warehouses

questions.explain: System tables include system.lakeflow.jobs, job_tasks, job_run_timeline, job_task_run_timeline, pipelines and pipeline_update_timeline.

questions.q: A continuous job runs three streams and one fails while the others run. Which setting makes the failed one retry on its own?

options.t: A duration warning on each task
Autoscaling turned on
options.why: Not for retries; and not recommended for streams.

options.t: Task retry mode set to On failure
Maximum concurrent runs set to 3, one per stream

questions.explain: With several continuous tasks in one job, a failed task retries on its own only if Task retry mode is On failure; otherwise the job waits for all tasks to fail.
